newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE to continue earnings growth in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: RWE to continue earnings growth in 96/97.

text.p: German diversified utility RWE AG said at the weekend that it expects net earnings to continue to improve in the current business year to the end of June 1996/97.
The Essen-based RWE wants to continue tracking the "helpful operating trend" established in the year to date, it said in its quarterly report to be published on Monday.
The utility reported group net profit of 180 million marks for the first quarter of 1996/97, from July to the end of September, an increase of 2.3 percent, as reported in a newspaper on Friday.
The group net profit figures were slightly below average because of seasonal factors, such as weak electricity demand in the summer, which mainly affected its energy business, the group said.

Cheaper electricity prices led to a 1.2 percent drop in turnover in RWE Energie to 4.82 billion marks in the quarter, but this was boosted by strong growth of 15 percent in petroleum and chemical sales to 6.76 billion marks.
Besides the seasonal factors, there were payments due on several large construction and capital expansion projects. Payment-due dates for such outgoings fall on June 31 or December 31.
The group's investments were set to rise clearly over the course of the year as RWE continued to expand its fledgling telecommunications interests.
RWE's telecoms business has been the focus of much attention after it suddenly left a strategic telecoms alliance with British Telecom Plc and its fellow German utility Viag AG in October.
RWE instead joined up with another huge German utility group, Veba AG, and BT's smaller rival, Cable & Wireless Plc.
In the first quarter, the group doubled its telecoms business to 226 million marks from 107 million marks in the same period a year ago.

Investments fell overall around 14 percent to 1.054 billion marks in the first quarter, down from 1.225 million a year previously, chiefly due to the acquisition of its Italian chemical unit CONDEA Augusta unit last year, RWE said.
In the business year 1995/96, RWE spent a total of 7.18 billion marks on acquisitions.
